title: The Number
editorialNotes: $2,913/yr is the EPA April 2025 household figure, the only number allowed hero treatment.
The brief's slide 3 bar-chart percentages (38/22/18/12/10) are visual direction, not slide copy, and are unsourced: not carried into the spec.

thread.element: torn-bill strip, one more piece torn away each slide

copy.heroNumberCaption: That's how much your family throws away in food every year.

copy.headline: The EPA published this number in April 2025.
items: For a household of 4, that's $2,913 — roughly 11% of total food spending.
copy.citation: EPA, "Estimating the Cost of Food Waste to American Consumers," April 2025

copy.headline: Where does it go?
items: Produce is #1. Leafy greens and berries spoil fastest.

copy.headline: The old stat was $1,500 per household — based on 2010 prices.
items: Food got more expensive AND we're still wasting the same percentage.
copy.citation: USDA 2014 (2010 price data) vs EPA April 2025

copy.headline: That's $56 a week.
copy.body: Imagine pulling $56 out of your wallet every Friday and dropping it in the trash. That's what's happening. Just slower.

copy.headline: The waste isn't dramatic. It's invisible.
items: A yogurt pushed to the back.
A leftover that never got reheated.

copy.headline: You don't have a grocery budget problem. You have a visibility problem.
